title: Spark's Artifact treats unfinished parameters as a declared state rather than omitting them
content:
Several of Spark's parameter documents exist but are deliberately empty of values. A.6.1.1.1.2.1.1.3.1.1.3 says the Genesis Account address "will be specified in a future iteration of the Spark Artifact." A.6.1.1.1.2.1.4.2.1.1.7.1 says SPK holders can stake, but "the rewards for staking will be specified in a future iteration." A.6.1.1.1.2.1.4.2.1.2.4 says the amount and nature of token-launch distributions "will be specified in a future iteration."

The pattern is that a pending decision gets its own addressable slot. The alternative — leaving the parameter out until it is decided — would make the Artifact look complete while hiding the gap, and would give a future amendment no fixed place to land.

This interacts directly with the Executor Transformation Primitive's Global Activation Status of `Inactive` (A.6.1.1.1.2.1.3.1.1): capability that has not yet been used is present in the document tree with a status marking it dormant, not absent from it.

The consequence for anyone reading an Agent Artifact is that presence of a section is not evidence of an operative rule. Status values and "future iteration" placeholders must be read as part of the specification, because a live-looking subtree can be entirely inert.
description: Genesis Account, staking rewards and token-launch distributions each appear as named documents whose content is 'will be specified in a future iteration', keeping the gap visible and addressable.
